The Checked Documentation Surface — static sign-off mock

Six surfaces, twenty-three declared states, two viewports, one theme: 46 frames. Every frame is drawn at its real declared width with content at the density the budget actually permits, and every density number under a frame is counted off the source pane beneath it rather than asserted beside a picture — so a budget that cannot hold shows up here instead of at implementation time. Two of them do not hold; see the findings below.

Nothing here is a live component import, because there is nothing to import: this repository tracks no stylesheet and owns no DOM. The mock inlines the one theme the repository itself generates — rustdoc’s, produced by the gate’s own cargo doc step — and mirrors its real emitted markup and class contracts. Where every pixel came from lists each one and the check that resolved it.

Six things drawing this found that reading it did not

Each is a claim in _design.md that did not survive being resolved against a file in this worktree. They are listed here because a mock whose only output is a picture has wasted the one chance to find them before the code exists.

  1. The fixture page does not compile. _design.md:603 opens use happenstance_core::memory::MemoryEventStore;. memory is a private module — mod memory; at crates/happenstance-core/src/lib.rs:103, with the type re-exported at :122 — so the resolving path is happenstance_core::MemoryEventStore. The artifact ## The doctest offers as “the substitute for the mock” fails the very step this project adds. It is drawn as gate-narrative-compile-step / fail-broken-fence rather than described, and every other frame here uses the corrected path.
  2. The composed failure report ends on a line xtask never prints. _design.md:335 renders Error: 3 problem(s) in docs. The verified primitive is eprintln!("\nxtask failed: {err:#}") at xtask/src/main.rs:712, and under cargo xtask ci a second line follows from the parent process — bail!("{} failed with {status}", step.name) at main.rs:887 — because each step is spawned as its own cargo run -p xtask. Every gate frame here shows both lines. The design's ## Composition block is one line short of what a contributor sees.
  3. The 48-character location-prefix budget does not survive the compile surface. Observed by running cargo test -p xtask --doc -- --list in this worktree: a doctest is named xtask\src\../../standards/rust/00-prime-directives.md - constitution::prime_directives (line 102). The xtask\src\../../ prefix is 16 characters the budget does not count, so docs/adapters/happenstance-cloudflare.md reaches 56 characters on the compile surface while fitting comfortably on the checker surface. The budget is stated once, under “The terminal surface”, and both steps write to that terminal.
  4. The 60-character H1 budget is derived from the wrong width. ## Density budget justifies it as “At 70 columns with a two-column table and its borders, ~60 is what the left column can hold”. The arithmetic, computed from the rows this mock actually draws: the widest right-column cell is 22 characters (adapters/cloudflare.md), table overhead is 7, so the left column holds 41 characters at 70 columns — not 60. 60 is the figure for the wide width, where 71 fit. Either the budget drops to ~40, or the narrow width stops being the one the index is sized against. Compare narrative-tree-index / long-label @1440x900 against narrative-tree-index / narrow-70col @1024x768.
  5. Two citations in the primitive table are off by two lines. The success summary is at lint_constitution.rs:192 (the table says 194) and the terminal bail! is at :199 (the table says 198). Both strings are otherwise exact, and spec-trace does not read this file, so nothing would have caught it.
  6. === narrative pages === breaks the house naming convention. Every name in REQUIRED is a claim sentence — “the Rust constitution is internally consistent” (xtask/src/main.rs:466), and this project's own first step, “the narrative tree's examples compile”. A noun phrase reads as a category rather than a claim, and the banner is the only thing telling a reader which half failed. The frames render the design's declared text unchanged; the convention is worth re-deciding at sign-off.

narrative-tree-index

route: docs/README.md
pattern: two-column routing table, extended (docs/README.md:12-24)
states: populated · empty-tree · long-label · narrow-70col

narrative-page

route: docs/<page>.md
pattern: always-visible single-need page; no hidden panels (DT-7 (b))
states: default · scoped-inline · long-page-overflow · long-label · narrow-70col

narrative-scoped-page

route: docs/<topic>/<scope>.md
pattern: one page per scope, reached from the index (DT-7 (c))
states: default · orphan-unregistered · narrow-70col

gate-narrative-compile-step

route: cargo xtask ci → === the narrative tree's examples compile ===
pattern: one #[cfg(doctest)] module per page, so a failure names the page
states: pass · fail-broken-fence · fail-removed-item · fail-many

gate-narrative-checker-step

route: cargo xtask narrative
pattern: accumulate every problem, report in source order, count last
states: pass · fail-one · fail-many · fail-empty-tree · fail-hidden-marker · fail-long-path

rustdoc-reference-surface

route: target/doc/happenstance/index.html
pattern: unchanged — this project adds no affordance to it
states: unchanged
